items.samhita_patha: मृ॒त्योर॒हं ब्र॑ह्मचा॒री यदस्मि॑ नि॒र्याच॑न्भू॒तात्पुरु॑षं य॒माय॑। तम॒हं ब्रह्म॑णा॒ तप॑सा॒ श्रमे॑णा॒नयै॑नं॒ मेख॑लया सिनामि ॥
items.pada_patha: मृ॒त्यो: । अ॒हम् । ब्र॒ह्म॒ऽचा॒री । यत् । अस्मि॑ । नि॒:ऽयाच॑न् । भू॒तात् । पुरु॑षम् । य॒माय॑ । तम् । अ॒हम् । ब्रह्म॑णा । तप॑सा । श्रमे॑ण । अ॒नया॑ । ए॒न॒म् । मेख॑लया । सि॒ना॒मि॒ ॥१३३.३॥

commentaries.whitney:
Since I am death's student ( brahmacārín ), soliciting from existence
(? bhūtá ) a man ( púruṣa ) for Yama, him do I, by incantation ( bráhman ), by fervor, by toil, tie with this girdle.
commentaries.whitney_notes: It is the duty of a Vedic student to beg provision for his teacher. Ppp. begins b with bhūtāu niryācan . The comm. reads niryācam , explaining it as first person sing. (= yāce )! The result he takes to be "by this binding on of a girdle I impede the progress of my enemy." Pāda c has a redundant syllable.

items.samhita_patha_plain: मृत्योरहं ब्रह्मचारी यदस्मि निर्याचन्भूतात्पुरुषं यमाय। तमहं ब्रह्मणा तपसा श्रमेणानयैनं मेखलया सिनामि ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: मृत्यो: । अहम् । ब्रह्मऽचारी । यत् । अस्मि । नि:ऽयाचन् । भूतात् । पुरुषम् । यमाय । तम् । अहम् । ब्रह्मणा । तपसा । श्रमेण । अनया । एनम् । मेखलया । सिनामि ॥१३३.३॥

items.samhita_patha: श्र॒द्धाया॑ दुहि॒ता तप॒सोऽधि॑ जा॒ता स्वसा॒ ऋषी॑णां भूत॒कृतां॑ ब॒भूव॑। सा नो॑ मेखले म॒तिमा धे॑हि मे॒धामथो॑ नो धेहि॒ तप॑ इन्द्रि॒यं च॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Daughter of faith, born out of fervor, sister of the being-making seers was she; do thou, O girdle, assign to us thought ( matí ), wisdom; also assign to us fervor and Indra's power.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All the mss. (and both editions) accent babhū́va at end of b , as if a relative were expressed or implied in the line somewhere. The verse is really mixed triṣṭubh and jagatī ; ⌊ a is jagatī only by count; no in c looks like an intrusion⌋. ⌊As to the combination -sa ṛṣ- , see note to Prāt. iii. 46.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: श्रद्धाया दुहिता तपसोऽधि जाता स्वसा ऋषीणां भूतकृतां बभूव। सा नो मेखले मतिमा धेहि मेधामथो नो धेहि तप इन्द्रियं च ॥

items.samhita_patha: यां त्वा॒ पूर्वे॑ भूत॒कृत॒ ऋष॑यः परिबेधि॒रे। सा त्वं परि॑ ष्वजस्व॒ मां दी॑र्घायु॒त्वाय॑ मेखले ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thou whom the ancient being-making seers bound about, do thou embrace me, in order to length of life, O girdle.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यां त्वा पूर्वे भूतकृत ऋषयः परिबेधिरे। सा त्वं परि ष्वजस्व मां दीर्घायुत्वाय मेखले ॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒यं वज्र॑स्तर्पयतामृ॒तस्या॑वास्य रा॒ष्ट्रमप॑ हन्तु जीवि॒तम्। शृ॒णातु॑ ग्री॒वाः प्र शृ॑णातू॒ष्णिहा॑ वृ॒त्रस्ये॑व॒ शची॒पतिः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let this thunderbolt gratify itself with right (? ṛtásya ), let it smite down his kingdom, away his life; let it crush [his] neck, crush up his nape, as Cachīpati of Vritra.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अयं वज्रस्तर्पयतामृतस्यावास्य राष्ट्रमप हन्तु जीवितम्। शृणातु ग्रीवाः प्र शृणातूष्णिहा वृत्रस्येव शचीपतिः ॥

items.samhita_patha: अध॑रोऽधर॒ उत्त॑रेभ्यो गू॒ढः पृ॑थि॒व्या मोत्सृ॑पत्। वज्रे॒णाव॑हतः शयाम् ॥
items.pada_patha: अध॑र:ऽअधर: । उत्त॑रेभ्य: । गू॒ढ: । पृ॒थि॒व्या: । मा । उत् । सृ॒प॒त् । वज्रे॑ण । अव॑ऽहत: । श॒या॒म् ॥१३४.२॥

commentaries.whitney: Beneath, beneath them that are above, hidden, may he not creep out of the earth; let him lie smitten down by the thunderbolt.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊The mark which should divide a from b is not noted in W's collation-book.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: अधरोऽधर उत्तरेभ्यो गूढः पृथिव्या मोत्सृपत्। वज्रेणावहतः शयाम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: अधर:ऽअधर: । उत्तरेभ्य: । गूढ: । पृथिव्या: । मा । उत् । सृपत् । वज्रेण । अवऽहत: । शयाम् ॥१३४.२॥

items.samhita_patha: यो जि॒नाति॒ तमन्वि॑च्छ॒ यो जि॒नाति॒ तमिज्ज॑हि। जि॑न॒तो व॑ज्र॒ त्वं सी॒मन्त॑म॒न्वञ्च॒मनु॑ पातय ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whoever scathes, him seek thou after; whoever scathes, him smite; the crown of the scather, O thunderbolt, do thou cause to fall following after.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The last pāda is very obscure; it is rendered as if it meant an involving of the offender's crown ( sīmanta:=çiraso madhyadeça , comm.) in the fall of the thunderbolt (but the comm. explains anvañcam by anulomam! ). Ppp. reads sāyakas for tvam in c . The Prāt, gives an obiter dictum (iii. 43) on the derivation of sīmánta (or sīmánt ). The metrical definition ⌊bhurig anuṣṭup⌋ seems to be omitted in the Anukr.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यो जिनाति तमन्विच्छ यो जिनाति तमिज्जहि। जिनतो वज्र त्वं सीमन्तमन्वञ्चमनु पातय ॥

items.samhita_patha: यद॒श्नामि॒ बलं॑ कुर्व इ॒त्थं वज्र॒मा द॑दे। स्क॒न्धान॒मुष्य॑ शा॒तय॑न्वृ॒त्रस्ये॑व॒ शची॒पतिः॑ ॥
items.pada_patha: यत् । अ॒श्नामि॑ । बल॑म् । कु॒र्वे॒ । इ॒त्थम् । वज्र॑म् । आ । द॒दे॒ । स्क॒न्धान् । अ॒मुष्य॑ । शा॒तय॑न् । वृ॒त्रस्य॑ऽइव । शची॒ऽपति॑: ॥१३५.१॥

commentaries.whitney: When ( yát ) I eat, I make strength; thus do I take the thunderbolt, cutting to pieces ( çat ) the shoulders of him yonder, as Cachīpati of Vritra.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Skandhá 'shoulder' is always plural ⌊in AV.⌋, and so is not precisely equivalent to the word used to render it. Ppp. has for b , vajram anupātayati . Pāda b is deficient unless we read va-jṛ-am .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदश्नामि बलं कुर्व इत्थं वज्रमा ददे। स्कन्धानमुष्य शातयन्वृत्रस्येव शचीपतिः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यत् । अश्नामि । बलम् । कुर्वे । इत्थम् । वज्रम् । आ । ददे । स्कन्धान् । अमुष्य । शातयन् । वृत्रस्यऽइव । शचीऽपति: ॥१३५.१॥

items.samhita_patha: यत्पिबा॑मि॒ सं पि॑बामि समु॒द्र इ॑व संपि॒बः। प्रा॒णान॒मुष्य॑ सं॒पाय॒ सं पि॑बामो अ॒मुं व॒यम् ॥
items.pada_patha: यत् । पिबा॑मि । सम् । पि॒बा॒मि॒ । स॒मु॒द्र:ऽइ॑व । स॒म्ऽपि॒ब: । प्रा॒णान् । अ॒मुष्य॑ । स॒म्ऽपाय॑ । सम् । पि॒बा॒म॒: । अ॒मुम् । व॒यम् ॥१३५.२॥

commentaries.whitney: When I drink, I drink up, an up-drinker like the ocean; drinking up the breath of him yonder, we drink him up.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines samudrāi ’va in b , and reads, in c, d , saṁpivāṁ saṁpivāmy ahaṁ pivā .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यत्पिबामि सं पिबामि समुद्र इव संपिबः। प्राणानमुष्य संपाय सं पिबामो अमुं वयम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: यत् । पिबामि । सम् । पिबामि । समुद्र:ऽइव । सम्ऽपिब: । प्राणान् । अमुष्य । सम्ऽपाय । सम् । पिबाम: । अमुम् । वयम् ॥१३५.२॥

items.samhita_patha: यद्गिरा॑मि॒ सं गिरा॑मि समु॒द्र इ॑व संगि॒रः। प्रा॒णान॒मुष्य॑ सं॒गीर्य॒ सं गि॑रामो अ॒मुं व॒यम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: When I swallow, I swallow up, a swallower-up like the ocean; swallowing up the breath of him yonder, we swallow him up.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for c, d , prāṇam amuṣya saṁgiraṁ saṁgirāmy ahaṁ giraṁ . The accent gírāmi in our text is doubtless wrong (read girā́mi ), but it is read by all the authorities, and accordingly is adopted in both editions.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यद्गिरामि सं गिरामि समुद्र इव संगिरः। प्राणानमुष्य संगीर्य सं गिरामो अमुं वयम् ॥

items.samhita_patha: दे॒वी दे॒व्यामधि॑ जा॒ता पृ॑थि॒व्याम॑स्योषधे। तां त्वा॑ नितत्नि॒ केशे॑भ्यो॒ दृंह॑णाय खनामसि ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thou art born divine on the divine one, [namely] the earth, O herb; thee here, O down-stretcher, we dig in order to fix the hair.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. explains the plant addressed to be the kācamācī etc.; nitatnī apparently not the name, but an epithet, "sending its roots far down" ( nyakprasaraṇaçīlā , comm.).

items.samhita_patha_plain: देवी देव्यामधि जाता पृथिव्यामस्योषधे। तां त्वा नितत्नि केशेभ्यो दृंहणाय खनामसि ॥

commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. strangely divides vss. 2 and 3 differently, adding 3 a, b to 2, and leaving 3 c, d to form by themselves a verse. ⌊The Anukr. scans as 9 + 9. The "verse" seems to be prose.⌋

commentaries.whitney: What hair of thine falls down, and what one is hewn off with its root, upon it I now pour with the all-healing plant.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm., as well as all the mss. (and both editions), has the false form vṛçcáte (for vṛçcyáte ).

commentaries.whitney_notes: Or vītahavya may be understood (with the Anukr.) as an epithet, 'after the gods had enjoyed his oblations.' The comm. takes it as a proper name, as also ásitasya (= kṛṣṇakeçasyāi ’tatsaṁjñasya muneḥ ).

commentaries.whitney: To be measured with a rein were they, to be after-measured with a fathom: let the black hairs grow out of thy head like reeds.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Ppp. version, though corrupt, suggests no different reading. The comm., startled at the exaggeration implied in abhīçu , declares it to mean "finger." In d , asitā́s is read by all the mss., and consequently by both editions; it apparently calls for emendation to ásitās , and is so translated kṛṣṇavarṇāḥ , comm.). The Anukr. seems to admit the contraction naḍe ’va in 2 c , 3 c .

commentaries.whitney_notes: Yāmaya , in b , is yamaya in pada -text, by Prāt. iv. 93.

commentaries.whitney: Thou art listened to, O herb, as the most best of plants; make thou now this man for me impotent ( klībá ), opaçá -wearing.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The opaçá is some head-ornament worn distinctively by women (comm. strīvyañjanam ). Geldner holds that opaça , kurīra (vs. 2), and kumba (vs. 3) all mean alike 'horn.' Ppp. reads pāuruṣam in c . The comm. does not attempt to identify the plant addressed.

items.samhita_patha: क्ली॒बं कृ॑ध्योप॒शिन॒मथो॑ कुरी॒रिणं॑ कृधि। अथा॒स्येन्द्रो॒ ग्राव॑भ्यामु॒भे भि॑नत्त्वा॒ण्ड्यौ᳡ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Do thou make him impotent, opaçá -wearing, likewise make him kurī́ra -wearing; then let Indra with the (two) pressing-stones split both his testicles.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. gives kṛtvā for kṛdhi in a (combining kṛtvo ’p- ), and reads throughout klīva and opaçu; in c, d it has ubhābhyām asya gr. indro bhinaitv ā . The comm. explains kurīra as = keça , and quotes from TS. iv. 1. 5 3 the phrase sinīvālī́ sukapardā́ sukurīrā́ svāupaçā́; and also, from an unknown source, stanakeçavatī strī syāl lomaçaḥ puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ .

commentaries.whitney: Impotent one, I have made thee impotent; eunuch ( vádhri ), I have made thee eunuch; sapless one, I have made thee sapless; the kurī́ra and the kúmba we set down upon his head.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. explains kurīra here as 'a net of hair' ( keçajāla ) and kumba as 'its ornament' ( tadābharaṇam ), and he quotes from ĀpÇS. x. 9. 5 the sentence atra patnīçirasi kumbakurīram adhy ūhate . Both words plainly signify some distinctively womanish head-dress or ornament. Ppp. reads (as also our P.s.m.) kumbham in e ; and, for c , arasaṁ tvā ’karam arasā ’raso ’si .

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines amuṣyā ’dhi in d (but perhaps the true saṁhitā -reading?). ⌊Ppp. has a gap in the place where our çamyayā stands.⌋

commentaries.whitney: As women split reeds with a stone for a cushion, so do I split thy member, on yon woman's loins.
commentaries.whitney_notes: In this and the preceding verse, the comm. strangely connects muṣkáyos with the preceding noun ( nāḍyāù , çépas ) and supplies çilāyās with amúṣyās .

items.samhita_patha: यौ व्या॒घ्रावव॑रूढौ॒ जिघ॑त्सतः पि॒तरं॑ मा॒तरं॑ च। तौ दन्तौ॑ ब्रह्मणस्पते शि॒वौ कृ॑णु जातवेदः ॥

commentaries.whitney: The (two) tigers that, having grown down, desire to devour father and mother—those (two) teeth, O Brahmaṇaspati, make thou propitious, O Jātavedas.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Our P.M.W. read kṛṇuhi in d . Ppp., instead of d , gives the refrain of 2, 3: mā hiṅs- etc.

commentaries.whitney: Eat ye (two) rice; eat ye barley; then beans, then sesame; this is your deposited ( níhita ) portion for treasuring, ye (two) teeth; do not injure father and mother.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Instead of atho māṣam in b , Ppp. has māṣām attam; it begins c with sa for eṣa , and reads -dheyam in d . The comm. paraphrases ratnadheyāya by ramaṇīyaphalāya . The verse (8 + 8 : 8 + 7 + 11 = 42) is but ill-defined by the Anukr. ⌊It is really an anuṣṭubh with d catalectic, and with a triṣṭubh refrain.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Invoked [are] the two conjoint, pleasant, very propitious teeth; let what is terrible of your selves ( tanū́ ) go away elsewhere, ye teeth; do not injure father and mother.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads aghorāu sayujā saṁvidānāu , and adds at the end anyatra vāṁ tanvo ghoratn astu . The comm. reads tanvās in c . The definition of the Anukr. fits the verse (7 + 8: 13 + 11) very ill. ⌊Whitney's notes show that he had suspected sayújāu to be a misreading for suyújāu , and the latter is the form actually given by the Index Verborum; but further notes show that Bp. and the Anukr. read sa- . With them agree SPP. and the comm. and Ppp. Correct the Index accordingly.⌋

items.samhita_patha: वा॒युरे॑नाः स॒माक॑र॒त्त्वष्टा॒ पोषा॑य ध्रियताम्। इन्द्र॑ आभ्यो॒ अधि॑ ब्रवद्रु॒द्रो भू॒म्ने चि॑कित्सतु ॥

commentaries.whitney: May Vāyu collect them; let Tvashṭar stay fast in order to [their] prosperity; may Indra bless them; let Rudra take care for [their] numbers.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Samā́karat (p. sam॰ā́karat ) might, of course, also be indicative ( sam-ā́-akarat ). Ppp., in c , combines indrā ”bhyo , and reads bruvat; in d , it has ‘va gachatu for cikitsatu . The comm. renders dhriyatām by dhārayatu , and d by pādāsyādirogaparihāreṇa bahvīḥ karotu .

items.samhita_patha_plain: वायुरेनाः समाकरत्त्वष्टा पोषाय ध्रियताम्। इन्द्र आभ्यो अधि ब्रवद्रुद्रो भूम्ने चिकित्सतु ॥

commentaries.whitney: With the red knife ( svádhiti ), make thou a pair ( mithuná ) on [their] two ears; the Açvins have made the mark; be that numerous by progeny.

items.samhita_patha: यथा॑ च॒क्रुर्दे॑वासु॒रा यथा॑ मनु॒ष्या᳡ उ॒त। ए॒वा स॑हस्रपो॒षाय॑ कृणु॒तं लक्ष्मा॑श्विना ॥

commentaries.whitney: As the gods and Asuras made [it], as human beings also, so, O Açvins, make ye the mark, in order to thousand-fold prosperity.

items.samhita_patha: उच्छ्र॑यस्व ब॒हुर्भ॑व॒ स्वेन॒ मह॑सा यव। मृ॑णी॒हि विश्वा॒ पात्रा॑णि॒ मा त्वा॑ दि॒व्याशनि॑र्वधीत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Rise up ( ut-çri ), become abundant ( bahú ) with thine own greatness, O barley; ruin ( mṛ ) all receptacles; let not the bolt from heaven smite thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Instead of mṛṇīhi in c , the comm. reads vṛṇīhi , which he says is, 'by letter-substitution,' for pṛṇīhi 'fill'! Pṛṇīhi would be an easier reading, and was conjectured by Ludwig, and before him by Aufrecht (KZ. xxvii. 218). ⌊Griffith and Bl., 'fill them till they burst.'⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: उच्छ्रयस्व बहुर्भव स्वेन महसा यव। मृणीहि विश्वा पात्राणि मा त्वा दिव्याशनिर्वधीत् ॥

commentaries.whitney: Where we appeal unto thee, the divine barley that listens, there ( tát ) rise up, like the sky; be unexhausted, like the ocean.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm., in b , reads tatra and achavad- .

items.samhita_patha: अक्षि॑तास्त उप॒सदोऽक्षि॑ताः सन्तु रा॒शयः॑। पृ॒णन्तो॒ अक्षि॑ताः सन्त्व॒त्तारः॑ स॒न्त्वक्षि॑ताः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Unexhausted be thine attendants (? upasád ), unexhausted thy heaps; thy bestowers be unexhausted; thy eaters be unexhausted.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The comm. explains upasadas as here rendered (= upagantāraḥ karmakarāḥ ); the translators conjecture 'piles,' a meaning which cannot properly be found in the word. By a strangely unequal division, the thirteenth and last anuvāka is made to consist of 18 hymns and 64 verses; the quoted Anukr. says yaḥ paraḥ sa catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ . The fifteenth prapāṭhaka ends with the book. Some of the mss. sum up the book correctly as containing 142 hymns and 454 verses.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अक्षितास्त उपसदोऽक्षिताः सन्तु राशयः। पृणन्तो अक्षिताः सन्त्वत्तारः सन्त्वक्षिताः ॥
